# CHIEF SCOUT — CYCLE 008 MOHAMED BRIEF
**Date:** Monday 9 Nov 2026 · Window: 2 Nov → 9 Nov 2026 (the 5 Nov pulse is folded in)

## CHIEF SCOUT — WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
- **One genuinely exciting find: Déploya Robotics (Lausanne).** It's an EPFL robotics team that turns building scaffolding into a track for robots. They incorporated as a company on 28 Oct, and the registry notice went public this week. No professional investor has backed them yet.
- **Two more worth a look, both in quantum hardware:** QMunicate (Munich, a Max Planck spin-off that links quantum computers together) and Rhonexum (Lausanne, chips that run at ultra-cold temperatures inside quantum computers). Rhonexum has just landed its first commercial order and is raising its next round now.
- **Updates on names you know:** Dream Machines' founder says a demo turned into a likely paid pilot. PolaSight won a CHF 100k loan, and its CTO won his Falling Walls Lab category. Linque didn't win at Falling Walls, and Herakles is still not a GmbH.
- **What to do:** if you only do one thing this week, research Déploya's founders and check it against Project A's pipeline. It's the cleanest "before the first round" case we've had in weeks.
- **Overall: a solid cycle, better than last week.** All three new cards came from primary sources (company registries, university news and grant pages), not funding headlines. Most funding news this week was already too late for us (for example microagi's $55m seed).

---

## INVESTIGATE NOW

### 1. Déploya Robotics Sàrl (Ecublens/Lausanne, Switzerland)
- **What do they do?** Putting up scaffolding and fitting building façades (the outer wall panels) is slow, manual and dangerous. Déploya builds a fold-out grid, inspired by origami, that goes up a building quickly. Small robots then ride along it, project the architect's drawings onto the wall and show workers exactly where to drill. Later, the robots are meant to do the drilling and panel fitting themselves.
- **Why did you find them?** Through the Swiss company register. "Déploya Robotics Sàrl" was newly registered at EPFL Innovation Park (statutes dated 28 Oct 2026, CHF 20k capital), with a well-known EPFL robotics professor among its shareholders.
- **Why is this interesting?** Façade work is about 35–60% of total façade cost, according to EPFL's write-up. About 500 Swiss workers are seriously hurt each year in scaffolding-related accidents (also EPFL's figure). Construction is one of the least automated big industries, and Déploya enters through a narrow first task (layout projection and checks) that it can sell before full automation works.
- **Why might Mohamed be early?** So far they have only grants and prizes: an EPFL Ignition Grant (2025), Venture Kick stages 1 and 2 (CHF 50k in total, May 2026) and an EPFL InnoGrant (CHF 100k). There's no professional VC money yet. They only just formed a company, which is usually the step right before a first round. They told Venture Kick they already have letters of intent (non-binding interest from customers) and "early investor discussions".
- **Why might Project A care?** It's B2B robotics in a huge, under-automated market, with a product that can grow from one task into a platform. That fits Project A's Industrial Autonomy theme.
- **What is special about the founders?** Thomas Estier (business and fundraising) co-founded two Swiss robotics companies, BlueBotics (2001) and Rovenso (2016). He was also EPFL's deputy vice-president for innovation. Dr Jan Petrš (technology) is an architect turned roboticist, with a PhD in construction robotics and a postdoc at EPFL. Prof. Dario Floreano, whose lab spun out senseFly and Flyability, is an adviser and holds 5% of the company.
- **What evidence do we actually have?**
  - ✅ Registry entry (SOGC, CHE-215.188.652): shareholders Petrš 57%, Estier 38%, Floreano 5%. EPFL news confirms the InnoGrant, Venture Kick confirms its grants, and the company website lists the team.
  - ⚠️ The "10x faster" and "zero errors" claims are marketing, not tested. Estier's earlier exits (what happened to BlueBotics and Rovenso) are not verified here.
  - ❓ Round size and timing, who the investors in those "discussions" are, and whether any pilot customer is named. The first industrial pilot is planned for 2027.
- **What could be wrong with the case?** Construction is slow to buy new technology, and robots on building sites have humbled many teams. It's still a prototype, and real use is about a year away.
- **Project A fit:** Industrial Autonomy · likely about to raise a first round, no lead announced (strongest timing signal) · CH (lower Project A base rate) · B2B · the portfolio has construction software (Vestigas, Copay) but no construction robotics. No direct product overlap was found, but this isn't a conflict clearance.
- **Chief Scout verdict: 🔥 VERY INTERESTING.** It has an experienced repeat founder, a top robotics lab behind it and a company formed only days ago, all before any VC money.
- **What should Mohamed do?** → Research founder (start with Thomas Estier), then check for a Project A conflict.

### 2. QMunicate GmbH (Garching/Munich, Germany)
- **What do they do?** Today's quantum computers are small. Instead of building one giant machine, QMunicate builds the hardware that links many smaller ones, using single atoms and particles of light, so they work like one bigger computer. Think of it as networking cables and routers, but for quantum computers.
- **Why did you find them?** By checking Munich quantum and Max Planck spin-offs, a gap I promised to cover after we missed Quint. It's listed as a 2026 startup at gate Garching, a local startup centre, and pitched at the Quantum World Congress on 1 Oct.
- **Why is this interesting?** It comes out of about 25 years of research in Prof. Gerhard Rempe's group at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, one of the world's leading groups in this area. The CTO says there's a pilot lined up with an unnamed company that builds quantum computers from atoms, plus a planned long-distance trial with Deutsche Telekom.
- **Why might Mohamed be early?** They've raised only about €330k so far, according to the CTO on stage, and he said they'll seek more investment. That makes it pre-institutional, with a round coming.
- **Why might Project A care?** It's Munich (the highest-weight city) with world-class science. If quantum computers scale by being linked together, the company that owns the link becomes very valuable.
- **What is special about the founders?** Maya Büki (CEO) and Dr Gianvito Chiarella (CTO), both from the Rempe group. Prof. Rempe is the scientific adviser.
- **What evidence do we actually have?**
  - ✅ gate Garching lists the company (founded 2026, the two founders, Max Planck origin), and the conference write-up quotes the CTO.
  - ⚠️ The €330k raised, the pilot and the Deutsche Telekom trial are all the CTO's own statements.
  - ❓ Who put in the €330k, the GmbH registration details, and when the round happens.
- **What could be wrong with the case?** It's very long-term: the next big technical milestone is about two years out. Paris-based Welinq and others are already funded in the same space. Quantum is also a field where Project A isn't active, so it may be off-thesis for them.
- **Project A fit:** Frontier Technologies · possible first round coming (company says it will raise; no lead) · Munich (highest weight) · B2B · no public overlap found.
- **Chief Scout verdict: 🟢 WORTH INVESTIGATING.** It has top-tier science and the right timing, but it's a deep, slow market.
- **What should Mohamed do?** → Research founder (check the Max Planck/Rempe links and who funded the €330k).

### 3. Rhonexum (Lausanne, Switzerland)
- **What do they do?** Quantum computers have to be kept colder than outer space, and today thousands of cables carry control signals in from room temperature. Rhonexum designs chips that work inside the freezer, which cuts the wiring and makes bigger machines possible.
- **Why did you find them?** It announced on 2 Nov a multi-year supply deal with ZuriQ (an ETH quantum spin-off), with a first order to be delivered by end-2026. Its Slush profile says it's raising a seed round.
- **Why is this interesting?** A paying customer this early is rare for quantum hardware. It comes out of EPFL's AQUA Lab, which is known for cold-temperature chip research.
- **Why might Mohamed be early?** It's partly early. They already raised a $1M pre-seed (Mar 2026, led by QDNL Participations) and got Venture Kick's full CHF 150k. The seed round now forming is the one to watch. A seed is the next, bigger round, here probably €2–5m (my estimate).
- **Why might Project A care?** It sells "picks and shovels" (parts every quantum-computer builder needs) whichever quantum approach wins.
- **What is special about the founders?** Vicente Carbon (CEO) and Dr Hung-Chi Han, both from EPFL's AQUA Lab.
- **What evidence do we actually have?** ✅ The ZuriQ deal (GGBa release), the $1M pre-seed (tech.eu), Venture Kick CHF 150k and the "raising seed" listing in the Swiss Slush kit. ⚠️ The order size is unknown. ❓ Who leads the seed and when.
- **What could be wrong with the case?** ZuriQ is a small startup itself, so one deal is thin proof. The quantum market is still early.
- **Project A fit:** Frontier Technologies · pre-seed done (QDNL lead), seed forming now, so watch this round · CH (lower Project A base rate) · B2B · no public overlap found.
- **Chief Scout verdict: 🟢 WORTH INVESTIGATING.** A real customer and a live round, but quantum is outside Project A's usual map.
- **What should Mohamed do?** → Monitor until funding signal (Slush, 17–19 Nov, is the natural moment).

- The tech-momentum lane (arXiv/GitHub) found nothing for the 8th cycle in a row. My proposal to reshape it (P2) is still waiting for you.

## LOSS REPORT (Grok, mapping Cycle 008 packet -> intake contract v1.0)
- Mapped: 7 of 7 packet entities (3 CREATE NOW, 2 UPDATE, 2 MONITOR) and 6 of 6 events. Nothing refused. The 9 archived names were never in the packet's entities and are not submitted.
- external_id: the living packet has no stable entity key, so ids were minted as pz-scout:<slug> and pz-event:<slug>. Future packets will carry them from the start.
- recommended_action (contract enum): INVESTIGATE NOW + "research founder" -> research; UPDATE with a founder/conflict check -> review; MONITOR or "watch at Slush" -> watch. The verbatim packet values are kept in scout_assessment.
- intent: CREATE NOW -> create, UPDATE -> update; MONITOR entities have no intent (the contract enum has no monitor value).
- stage: the packet's free-text stage is kept verbatim in scout_assessment.stage_note; the enum is a lossy best fit (Rhonexum and 4QT set to pre_seed because their seed is still forming).
- claims: FACT/INFERENCE/UNKNOWN were reconstructed from the brief's evidence ticks; the packet does not label claims itself.
- Déploya SOGC evidence is the shab.ch homepage, not a deep link to the notice (the packet stored only the homepage).
- Dream Machines: the HRB court is not stated in the packet, so the Handelsregister id is sent without a court name. Location sent as Munich (registered seat); Zurich operations remain in the scout_assessment text only.
- 4QT: city unknown (country only); no signal_date in the packet.
- Events: start dates only (no times evidenced). End dates for Slush (19 Nov) and Big Berlin Hack (29 Nov) come from the brief. Event source_scouts are not recorded in the packet. The CNRS RISE results (27 Nov) appear in the brief but not in the packet's events and are not submitted.
- Envelope summary fields (unique_entities, convergence_count, zero_finding_lanes, the registry-completion notes) have no structured home; they are only in this text.
